collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A villager writes a list of landmarks for the way home and a friend wants to add some: let them add some, or keep it serious.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is going to a village two days' walk away and is afraid of getting lost on the way back. So (subject.he/she) has written a list of landmarks on a strip of bark: "Big rock. Left at the split tree. Stream. Second stream \(smaller\). Hill that looks like a sleeping pig." (friend) reads it over (subject.his/her) shoulder and asks for a turn with the charcoal.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) takes the charcoal back. This is important. (subject.He/she) follows the list carefully there and back, and it works perfectly, except that from the other direction the hill looks nothing like a sleeping pig. It looks like a sleeping goat. (subject) corrects the list for next time.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (friend) adds a few of (friend.his/her) own: "Tree that looks surprised." "The place where you'll wish you'd brought more water." "Halfway: have a snack." (subject) pretends to be annoyed. On the way home, (subject.he/she) follows every one, and finds the surprised tree, and laughs out loud alone on the path.
